findings.evidence: The validator calls requireAtLeastOne for daily-limit, max-input-chars, max-tokens, history-size and max-concurrent. It never checks connect-timeout-ms or read-timeout-ms (defaults 2000 and 20000), the range of temperature (default 0.2), or an upper bound on max-input-chars. V7 has question VARCHAR(4000) NOT NULL and the entity has @Column(nullable = false, length = 4000), while max-input-chars only has to be >= 1.
findings.why_it_matters: A timeout of 0 or a negative value is accepted at startup, and in many HTTP clients 0 means no timeout. A max-input-chars above 4000 passes startup validation but fails the chat_message insert after quota has been charged. An out-of-range temperature surfaces only as a vendor 400 per request.
findings.required_action: Add checks to the same aggregated list: both timeouts >= 1, temperature within the vendor's valid range, and max-input-chars <= 4000 (one named constant shared with the column length), with matching validator tests. May be deferred to the Phase 3 client wiring if recorded.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED to phase-03 (client wiring); recorded in plan.md Risks.

findings.evidence: chat_message has session_id UUID NOT NULL, student_id UUID NOT NULL with no FOREIGN KEY to chat_session (session_id, student_id). Session ownership (the IDOR guarantee in plan AD-07) rests on the chat_session PK plus application ordering.
findings.why_it_matters: The database cannot reject a chat_message whose student_id differs from the owner of its session_id, or whose session row does not exist.
findings.required_action: Consider UNIQUE (session_id, student_id) on chat_session and a composite FK from chat_message. If not wanted, record the decision (application-enforced ownership) in plan.md and verify the IDOR race test at Phase 3 on real Postgres.
findings.resolution: ACCEPTED AS DESIGN: no FK, because the locked phase-1 tests insert chat_message rows with random session ids. Ownership is application-enforced; Phase 3 adds a real-Postgres IDOR race test. Recorded in plan.md Risks.

findings.evidence: The three Spring Data repositories and the three entities are registered regardless of chat.ai.enabled. Only ChatAiConfig carries @ConditionalOnProperty.
findings.why_it_matters: Entities must stay mapped anyway because V7 always exists and ddl-auto is validate. Later phases must keep every service, controller and component behind the flag, and the 'disabled means no chat bean' tests should be scoped to non-JPA beans.
